content: Neomycin, polymyxin, and bacitracin are combined in a topical medication used to prevent minor skin injuries, such as cuts, scrapes, and burns, from becoming infected. These medications belong to a class of drugs known as antibiotics. They work by inhibiting the growth of bacteria. This medication is available as an ointment for application to the skin. It is typically used one to three times daily. While it is available without a prescription, your doctor may provide specific instructions for its use based on your medical condition. Follow the directions on the package or those provided by your doctor carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. This medication is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. You may use this medication to treat minor skin injuries. However, it should not be used for deep cuts, puncture wounds, animal bites, severe burns, or injuries affecting large areas of the body. For such injuries, contact your doctor or seek emergency medical attention, as alternative treatments may be necessary. If you use this medication for a minor skin injury and your symptoms do not improve within one week, stop using it and consult your doctor. Do not apply this medication to a child’s diaper area, especially if the skin is broken or raw, unless specifically instructed by a doctor. If directed to use it in this area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants. To apply the ointment, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 2. Clean the injured area with soap and water, then pat it dry with a clean towel. 3. Apply a small amount of the ointment (about the size of your fingertip) to the affected area. A thin layer is sufficient. Avoid touching the tip of the tube to your skin, hands, or any other surface. 4. Replace and tighten the cap immediately after use. 5. You may cover the treated area with a sterile bandage if desired. 6. Wash your hands again after application. This medication may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to neomycin, polymyxin, bacitracin, aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g., amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, paromomycin, tobramycin), zinc, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have a history of hearing problems or kidney disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Skin pain, irritation, burning, swelling, or redness Itching Rash Hives Red, scaly patches on the skin Difficulty breathing or swallowing Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Hoarseness Chest tightness Faintness or dizziness If you experience any unusual problems while using this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Do not ingest this medication. If someone swallows it, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If your doctor has instructed you to use this medication, keep all follow-up appointments. Contact your doctor if your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course. If you have any questions about this medication, consult your pharmacist.
